How is Martial Arts workout copy different from Boxing, Kickboxing, Wrestling, or Tai Chi?

Martial Arts workout copy covers general martial arts training session metrics — martial arts workout sessions, session summaries, heart rate during martial arts practice, active calories, and duration cards — 武术 / 武术训练 / 武术锻炼 / 武术运动. Boxing copy covers punch-focused ring or bag sessions — 拳击 / 拳击训练. Kickboxing copy covers kick/strike combat-cardio classes — 踢拳 / 踢拳训练. Wrestling copy covers mat takedown and period logging — 摔跤 / 垫上摔跤. Tai Chi copy covers slow-form movement sessions — 太极 / 太极训练. Each is a distinct Apple Watch workout type with its own listing scope when that workout leads your gallery.

How is Martial Arts workout copy different from Functional Strength Training, HIIT, or Fitness hub?

Martial Arts workout copy covers martial arts drill and training session cards — 武术 / 武术训练. Functional Strength Training and Traditional Strength copy covers rep counters and set logging — 功能性力量训练 / 力量训练 / 组数记录. HIIT copy covers interval timers and work/rest rounds — 高强度间歇训练 / 间歇计时. Fitness hub copy covers Activity rings and Training Load — 健身 / 活动闭环 / 训练负荷.

Which zh-Hans terms should Martial Arts workout listing copy use?

It depends on each frame. 武术 for general Martial Arts positioning. 武术训练 for structured Martial Arts Training sessions and drill libraries. 武术锻炼 for duration, heart-rate, calorie, and session-summary cards. 武术运动 for shorter subtitle packing. AppLocale picks idiomatic phrasing from your English source — not 拳击 on martial arts drill overlays, not 踢拳 on martial arts heart-rate frames, not 摔跤 on standing drill frames, not 太极 on combat session summaries, and not 力量训练 on martial arts duration cards unless each frame is labeled honestly.
